Config.PushingMenuHint: Configure bane damage, Stress Dice, Doom Points, and Conditions for pushed rolls.
Config.PushingIntro: Choose whether pushed-roll banes cause damage, then enable the other costs and consequences used by this world.
Config.RuleVariantsMenuHint: Choose the SRD variants used for encumbrance, consumables, Critical Injuries, ammunition, and initiative.
Config.RuleVariantsIntro: These world-level choices define which SRD variant each shared equipment and combat workflow uses. Stored ratings are preserved when a mode is hidden.
Config.CharacterFeaturesMenuHint: Choose the optional resources and features shown on character sheets.
Config.CharacterFeaturesIntro: Enable only the optional character-sheet features needed by this world. Hidden data is preserved.
Config.CurrencyMenuHint: Enable a Character currency balance, rename it for this world, and choose which Item types show price fields.
Config.CurrencyIntro: Configure the world's currency terminology and Item pricing fields. Disabled or hidden values remain stored.
Config.PersonalityFieldsMenuHint: Choose and rename the structured personality fields used by Characters.
Config.PersonalityFieldsIntro: Enable the personality concepts used by this world and rename them to match the game. Disabled values remain stored on Actors.
Config.OptionalSubsystemsMenuHint: Enable or disable Magic, Vehicles and Chases, and Travel for this world.
Config.OptionalSubsystemsIntro: These independent world-level switches enable the full rules and sheet controls for each optional subsystem. Hidden data is preserved.
Config.AttributeNamesMenuHint: Rename the four core Attributes to suit this world.
Config.AttributeNamesIntro: Set the world-specific display name for each of the four core Attributes.
Config.HeaderFieldsMenuHint: Configure the optional identity fields shown at the top of character sheets.
Config.HeaderFieldsHint: Enable only the identity fields this world needs and give each one a world-specific label.
Config.Saved: World settings saved. Reload the world to ensure every sheet and rule component uses the new settings.

DiceSystem.Name: Core dice system
DiceSystem.Hint: Choose D6 dice pools or the stepped-dice variant for Attribute and Skill ratings and rolls. Changing this setting does not erase ratings from the other variant.

StepModifierMethod.Name: Stepped Dice modifier method
StepModifierMethod.Hint: Use detailed numerical die steps or the faster Advantage/Disadvantage alternative. This setting only affects Stepped Dice rolls.

StepRatingLabelStyle.Name: Stepped rating labels
StepRatingLabelStyle.Hint: Choose whether stepped-rating menus display rating letters or die sizes. The stored ratings and dice rolled are unchanged.

TrackSuccessfulSkillUse.Name: Track successful Skill use
TrackSuccessfulSkillUse.Hint: Show a checkbox for marking Skills used successfully since the character's last advancement.

Currency.Name: Use Character currency
Currency.Hint: Show a renameable Cash, Money, Credits, or similar balance on Character sheets and enable configured Item price fields.
Currency.LabelHint: The world-specific name displayed for the Character balance, such as Cash, Money, Credits, Gold, or Resources.
Currency.ItemTypesHint: Choose which Item types display a price field while currency is enabled.
Currency.ItemTypeHint: Show a price field for this Item type while currency is enabled.

HarmModel.Name: Damage model
HarmModel.Hint: Choose whether harm reduces Health and Resolve, Health only, is tracked with Conditions, or reduces the rolled Attribute directly.

EncumbranceMode.Name: Encumbrance rules
EncumbranceMode.Hint: Choose how carried Item weight is calculated on Character and NPC sheets.

ConsumableMode.Name: Consumable rules
ConsumableMode.Hint: Track each unit with Item quantity, or give each Consumable a Supply rating.

CriticalInjuryTrigger.Name: Critical Injury trigger
CriticalInjuryTrigger.Hint: Choose one of the SRD example events which automatically rolls a Critical Injury. Select the zero-value or Conditions option that matches the world's Damage model. The pushed-damage exception applies to those three options.
CriticalInjuryTrigger.ConditionsBroken: Broken by physical or mental Conditions
CriticalInjuryTrigger.DamageThreshold: Attack damage reaches the Weapon Crit threshold
CriticalInjuryTrigger.SuccessThreshold: Attack rolls two or more successes

AmmunitionMode.Name: Ammunition rules
AmmunitionMode.Hint: Choose whether attacks ignore ammunition, count rounds, make Supply rolls, or roll Ammo Dice using Rate of Fire.
AmmunitionMode.AmmoDice: Ammo Dice and Rate of Fire

InitiativeMode.Name: Initiative rules
InitiativeMode.Hint: Use the public ten-card draw, or keep other combatants' card values hidden and redraw every round.

StressDice.Name: Use Stress Dice
StressDice.Hint: Add D6 Stress Dice equal to current Stress and gain one Stress Die when pushing. A bane on a Stress Die triggers panic.

PushBaneDamageMode.Name: Attribute and Gear bane damage
PushBaneDamageMode.Hint: Choose whether banes remaining after a push inflict harm using the selected Damage model. Choose no bane damage for a Stress Dice-only, Conditions-only, Doom-only, or combined pushing variant.
PushBaneDamageMode.None: No bane damage (enabled pushing options only)

DoomPoints.Name: Use Doom Points
DoomPoints.Hint: Each pushed roll adds one point to the shared Doom pool. Everyone can view the dedicated Doom panel; only configured manager roles can gain, spend, or reset the pool.

DoomManagerRole.Name: Minimum Doom manager role
DoomManagerRole.Hint: Choose the lowest built-in Foundry User Role allowed to manage Doom Points. Ordinary Player-role users cannot be selected.
DoomManagerRole.Trusted: Trusted Player, Assistant GM, and Game Master

Conditions.Name: Apply a Condition when pushing
Conditions.Hint: A pushed roll immediately applies a chosen physical or mental Condition matching the rolled Attribute. Condition tracking remains available automatically when the Conditions damage model is selected.

Willpower.Name: Use Willpower
Willpower.Hint: Show and track Willpower on Character and NPC sheets. Pushing normally grants one Willpower; when pushed-roll banes use Attribute Damage, each point actually lost grants one instead.

CriticalInjuries.Name: Track Critical Injuries
CriticalInjuries.Hint: Show Critical Injury Items, injury-table controls, and legacy injury notes on Character and NPC sheets.

Experience.Name: Track Experience Points
Experience.Hint: Show the Experience tab, advancement controls, and award/spend ledger on Character and NPC sheets.

Magic.Name: Use Magic / Spells
Magic.Hint: Enable spellcasting, discipline ranks, Willpower costs, safe and chance casting, overcharging, and Magic Mishaps.

Vehicles.Name: Use Vehicles, Mounts & Chases
Vehicles.Hint: Enable ground and aerial Vehicles, Mount Actors, mounted combat and travel, secret multi-participant chases, automated obstacles, and their related sheet tools.

Travel.Name: Use Travel
Travel.Hint: Enable the shared day, shift, and weather clock; travel activities; supply gains; vehicle journeys; and travel mishaps.

Field1.EnabledHint: Show the first custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field1.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the first custom identity field.

Field2.EnabledHint: Show the second custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field2.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the second custom identity field.

Field3.EnabledHint: Show the third custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field3.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the third custom identity field.

Field4.EnabledHint: Show the fourth custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field4.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the fourth custom identity field.

Field5.EnabledHint: Show the fifth custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field5.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the fifth custom identity field.

Field6.EnabledHint: Show the sixth custom identity field at the top of Character and NPC sheets.
Field6.LabelHint: The world-specific display name for the sixth custom identity field.

strength.Name: Attribute 1 label (physical)
strength.Hint: The display name for the first physical attribute. The default is Strength.

agility.Name: Attribute 2 label (physical)
agility.Hint: The display name for the second physical attribute. The default is Agility.

wits.Name: Attribute 3 label (mental)
wits.Hint: The display name for the first mental attribute. The default is Wits.

empathy.Name: Attribute 4 label (mental)
empathy.Hint: The display name for the second mental attribute. The default is Empathy.

PersonalityFields.EnabledHint: Show this structured personality field on Character sheets.
PersonalityFields.LabelHint: Rename this personality concept for the current world.
PersonalityFields.FieldHint: Show or hide the {field} field and choose its world-specific label.

Actor.SkillHint: Create Skill Items in the sidebar, assign their linked attribute, then drag them onto this sheet.
Actor.RemoveSkillConfirm: Remove {skill} from this Actor? The reusable world Skill will not be deleted.
Actor.RemoveCriticalInjuryConfirm: Remove {injury} from this Actor? The reusable world Item will not be deleted.
Actor.BrokenConditionHint: The fourth Condition of one category marks the Actor Broken. Clear the corresponding box after recovery.
Actor.NotesPlaceholder: Write character and session notes here.

Item.BrokenGearHint: This item is broken and cannot provide a roll modifier until its Reliability is repaired.
Item.ExactConsumableHint: This world tracks individual units using the Quantity field above.
Item.DamageOnSkills: Skills which inflict damage when rolled
Item.BlockedAttributes: Attributes whose rolls are prevented (comma-separated keys)

ItemEffects.Title: Item Effects
ItemEffects.Empty: This Item has no configured effects.
ItemEffects.Hint: Most effects apply only while this Item is embedded on an Actor. Carryable Items must be equipped; Specialities and Critical Injuries must be active. Selectable roll modifiers are offered in the roll dialogue; automatic modifiers are always applied. Doom Expenditure effects on world Items are published in the shared Doom panel.
ItemEffects.CapacityMultiplierHint: Multiplies the Actor's final carry limit while this Item is active.
ItemEffects.InitiativeChoiceHint: {actor} drew additional initiative cards from active Item effects. Choose one card to keep.
ItemEffects.HitInterceptionHint: Allows this Actor to roll the selected Skill and take a nearby ally's hit without spending an action. The roll can be pushed. Mobility is used when no Skill is configured.
ItemEffects.CoupDeGraceHint: Allows this Actor to perform a coup de grâce without first rolling Empathy.
ItemEffects.WillpowerActivationHint: When this Item is active on an Actor, its owner can spend the configured Willpower cost to announce and activate this effect.
ItemEffects.DoomExpenditureHint: When active on an Actor, an authorised Doom manager can spend the shared cost from that Actor's sheet. A world Item with this effect is listed in the shared Doom panel.

Roll.AcceptedHint: This roll has been accepted and can no longer be pushed.
Roll.AcceptNotAllowed: Only the roll's author or a GM can accept it.
Roll.AcceptFailed: The roll could not be accepted.
Roll.PushCardHint: Open the Push Roll dialog to choose which eligible dice to reroll.
Roll.PushDialogHint: Select the dice to reroll. Unsuccessful dice are selected by default; successful dice may also be selected.
Roll.NoPushDice: Every die is a bane, so none can be rerolled.
Roll.NoPushDiceStress: The existing dice are all banes, but pushing will add one new Stress Die.
Roll.SelectPushDice: Select at least one non-bane die to reroll.
Roll.PushNotAllowed: Only the roll's author or a GM can push it.
Roll.PushFailed: The pushed roll could not be completed.
Roll.BaneBreakdown: Banes — Attribute: {attribute}, Skill: {skill}, Advantage: {advantage}, Gear: {gear}, Artifact: {artifact}, Stress: {stress}
Roll.NoConditionAvailable: All matching Conditions are already marked; another Condition breaks the Actor.
Roll.StressGained: Gained 1 Stress and added a new Stress Die.
Roll.StressManual: Gain 1 Stress; the Actor could not be updated automatically.
Roll.PanicTriggered: Panic triggered: at least one Stress Die rolled a bane.
Roll.AttributeLost: {attribute} was reduced by {count} from Attribute banes.
Roll.HarmManual: Apply {count} points of pushing harm manually.
Roll.GearDamageManual: Reduce the relevant gear bonus by {count}; the roll does not identify a specific Gear Item.
Roll.GearDamaged: {gear} lost {count} Gear rating; its current rating is {bonus}.
Roll.GearBroken: {gear} lost {count} Gear rating and is broken.
Roll.ConditionBroken: All {group} Conditions were already marked; the Actor is broken and suffers an appropriate critical injury.
Roll.DoomPointRequested: Requested 1 Doom Point for the shared GM pool.
Roll.WillpowerManual: Gain {count} Willpower; the Actor could not be updated automatically.
Roll.ConsequenceUpdateFailed: Some consequences could not be written to the Actor; verify them manually.
Roll.PushCostHint: Configured world consequences have been applied where the Actor could be updated safely.
Roll.MagicReplacementSuccesses: Magic replaces this roll with {count} automatic success(es)
Roll.AutomaticReplacementHint: This spell replaces the dice roll; difficulty, help, gear, and other modifiers do not change its automatic successes.
Roll.NoSpecialtyModifiers: No active Specialties have a configured modifier.
Roll.NoItemEffectModifiers: No active embedded Items have a matching roll modifier.
Roll.NoGearModifiers: No carried Gear or Weapons have a configured bonus.
Roll.PassiveCannotPush: This is a passive roll because the Actor is unaware or not actively taking an action. It cannot be pushed.
Roll.SecretRoll: Secret roll — result shown only to the GM
Roll.SecretRollForced: Secret passive roll — the result is shown only to the GM.
Roll.PassiveRollNotice: Passive roll — pushing is not allowed
Roll.ModifierHint: Difficulty, help, Specialties, Conditions, and other modifiers are cumulative. Selected Gear is kept as Gear Dice in dice-pool mode.
Roll.StepModifierCapped: The requested modifier was {requested}; the stepped-dice limits allowed {applied}.
Roll.AdvantageHint: Each positive source is an Advantage and each negative source is a Disadvantage. They cancel one-for-one; only one net Advantage or Disadvantage affects the roll.
Roll.AdvantageSingleDie: This roll started with only one base die. Advantage adds one matching die, while Disadvantage cannot reduce it further; the SRD recommends a minimum Skill rating of D when using this method.

Helping.MatchingAction: Each selected helper will spend one {action} when the roll is made.
Helping.SelectionHint: Select up to {maximum} physically present helpers. Each gives +1; the GM decides whether the help makes sense.
Helping.NoneAvailable: No mechanically capable helper tokens share this Actor's active Scene.
Helping.NotAllowed: Helpers are not allowed for this roll.
Helping.TooManyHelpers: No more than {maximum} Actors can help a single roll.
Helping.HelperUnavailable: A selected helper is no longer present or able to help.
Helping.ActionTypeRequired: Choose whether the supported combat action is Fast or Slow.
Helping.NotEnoughActions: {helper} does not have the required combat action remaining.
Helping.ActionSpendFailed: The helper combat actions could not be spent; the roll was cancelled.
Helping.GMRequired: An active GM is required to spend actions for helpers you do not own.
Helping.GMTimeout: The GM did not confirm the helper action spending in time; the roll was cancelled.

Attempts.Title: Only One Attempt
Attempts.GoalPlaceholder: For example: open the archive vault
Attempts.GoalHint: Enter the specific goal when the SRD's only-one-chance rule applies. After this roll, this Actor cannot try that goal again until the GM clears it. Combat rolls are never tracked.
Attempts.AlreadyAttempted: {actor} has already attempted “{goal}”. Try a different approach, wait for circumstances to change, let another Actor try, or ask the GM to clear the lock.
Attempts.SheetHint: Only a GM can clear these goals after circumstances substantially change.
Attempts.ClearFailed: The attempt lock could not be cleared.

Surprise.Title: Manoeuvres
Surprise.SheetHint: Target one token for a sneak attack. A GM can target several victims to resolve an ambush or grant surprise directly.
Surprise.SneakAttackSheetHint: Target one token to attempt a Stealth approach and prepare a sneak attack.
Surprise.CoupDeGraceSheetHint: Target one defenseless living Character or NPC. In combat this spends one Slow Action and may require an Empathy roll.
Surprise.CoupDeGraceBypassSheetHint: Target one defenseless living Character or NPC. In combat this spends one Slow Action; an active Item Effect bypasses the Empathy roll.
Surprise.AmbushSheetHint: As GM, target one or more victim tokens to resolve their secret passive Observation rolls and ambush initiative.
Surprise.ChooseInitiativeSheetHint: With an active Combat, choose any available initiative card for this surprising Actor.
Surprise.PendingSheet: A successful sneak attack is prepared against {target}. The next matching attack applies its surprise benefits.
Surprise.SneakAttackHint: {actor} attempts to approach {target} unnoticed. Choose the intended attack type before rolling Stealth.
Surprise.StealthMissing: The attacker needs a Stealth Skill Item.
Surprise.SneakRollSucceeded: The Stealth roll succeeded against {target}. Resolve it after any desired push.
Surprise.SneakRollFailed: The Stealth roll failed against {target}. Resolve it after any desired push.
Surprise.ResolveFailed: The surprise result could not be resolved.
Surprise.OwnerRequired: Only a GM or an owner of the attacker can resolve this sneak attack.
Surprise.SneakPrepared: {actor} surprises {target} and chooses initiative {card}. The next matching attack receives the sneak-attack benefits.
Surprise.PendingAttack: Prepared sneak attack against {target}: the target is unaware and cannot block a matching close-combat attack.
Surprise.KindMismatch: The prepared sneak attack was for a different attack type, so its benefits were not consumed.
Surprise.ChooseInitiativeHint: {actor} is fully surprising the enemy and may choose any available initiative card.
Surprise.CombatantRequired: Add the surprising Actor to the active Combat before choosing its initiative. Any prepared sneak attack remains available.
Surprise.GMDrawsOthers: The surprising Actor's card is set. A GM must draw initiative for the remaining combatants.
Surprise.CombatRequired: Create an active Combat before resolving ambush initiative.
Surprise.GMRequired: Only a GM can resolve an ambush for multiple victims.
Surprise.AmbushHint: Each of the {count} targeted victims makes a secret passive Observation roll. Failed victims receive the bottom initiative cards.
Surprise.WellPrepared: The attackers are well prepared (victims suffer −2)
Surprise.AmbushNeedsFreshInitiative: Ambush handling requires a fresh Combat with no initiative values assigned. Reset initiative first.
Surprise.SelectAmbushTargets: Target one or more victim tokens before resolving the ambush.
Surprise.AmbushTargetInvalid: Every ambush victim must be in the active Combat and have an Observation Skill Item.
Surprise.AmbushResolved: Ambush resolved: {failed} of {total} victims failed Observation and received randomly assigned bottom initiative cards. All others drew normally.

Bodyguard.Title: Bodyguard Interception
Bodyguard.Hint: Choose an Actor who can intercept the hit against {target}. Because this toolkit uses abstract range bands, confirm that the interceptor is within Short range.
Bodyguard.WithinShortRange: The interceptor is within Short range of the original target
Bodyguard.RangeRequired: Confirm that the Bodyguard is within Short range before rolling.
Bodyguard.NoneAvailable: No owned Actor on the active Scene has an active Hit Interception Item Effect and its configured Skill.
Bodyguard.RollSucceeded: {bodyguard} can intercept the hit against {target}. Resolve this after any desired push.
Bodyguard.RollFailed: {bodyguard} failed to intercept the hit against {target}. Resolve this after any desired push.
Bodyguard.NoHit: The attack no longer has any net successes to intercept.
Bodyguard.Intercepted: {bodyguard} dives in and takes the hit intended for {target}.
Bodyguard.NotIntercepted: {bodyguard} fails to intercept the hit intended for {target}.
Bodyguard.OwnerRequired: Only a GM or an owner of the intercepting Actor can resolve this roll.
Bodyguard.GMRequired: An active GM is required to attach this interception to another user's attack.
Bodyguard.Failed: The Bodyguard interception could not be completed.

Coup.Title: Coup de Grâce
Coup.Hint: {actor} is attempting to kill the defenseless {target} outright. In combat this spends one Slow Action.
Coup.BypassHint: An active Coup-de-grâce Item Effect bypasses the Empathy roll.
Coup.EmpathyHint: Roll the Empathy Attribute only. The coup de grâce can proceed only if the roll scores no successes; it cannot be pushed.
Coup.MechanicallyDefenseless: The target is mechanically Broken or helpless in a grapple.
Coup.ConfirmDefenseless: The GM has ruled that the target is otherwise defenseless
Coup.ConfirmKill: Confirm that this action will mark the target deceased
Coup.ColdBloodCost: A completed coup de grâce inflicts one point of mental harm on the executioner through the world's selected damage model. The Merciless example bypasses only the roll, matching its SRD wording.
Coup.Refused: {actor}'s Empathy prevents them from killing {target} in cold blood.
Coup.Killed: {actor} performs a coup de grâce. {target} is deceased.
Coup.AttackerUnavailable: A dead or Broken Actor cannot perform a coup de grâce.
Coup.InvalidTarget: A coup de grâce requires one living Character or NPC target other than the acting Actor.
Coup.ConfirmationRequired: Confirm both that the target is defenseless and that the action is lethal.
Coup.GMRequired: An active GM is required to mark an unowned target deceased.
Coup.GMFictionRequired: Only a GM or owner of the target can declare an otherwise healthy target defenseless. A player can request a coup de grâce against an unowned target once it is mechanically Broken or helpless.
Coup.GMRequested: The cold-blood consequence was applied. The GM has been asked to mark the target deceased.
Coup.GMConfirmHint: {actor} declared {target} defenseless without a mechanically Broken state. Confirm the fictional positioning before allowing the coup de grâce.

Opposed.DialogHint: Choose the Actor and test opposing {roll}.
Opposed.DefenderCannotPush: The opposing party cannot push this roll. The active party may push after seeing the result.
Opposed.NoActors: No Character or NPC Actors are available for you to roll as the opposition.
Opposed.NotAllowed: Only the active roll's author or a GM can start its opposed roll.
Opposed.Failed: The opposed roll could not be completed.
Opposed.Title: Opposed Roll Result
Opposed.ActiveWins: The active party wins by {margin} net successes.
Opposed.Tie: Tie: the active party normally fails.
Opposed.ActiveLoses: The active party fails; the opposition rolled more successes.
Opposed.PushHint: Each opposing success cancels one active success. Only the active party can push.

Advancement.AwardHint: Review the session for {actor}. Current XP: {current}.
Advancement.GMFinalSay: Each yes answer awards 1 XP. The GM has the final say on the award.
Advancement.NoXPAwarded: Select at least one question or enter additional XP.
Advancement.AdjustHint: Record a game-specific Experience award or spend for {actor}. Current XP: {current}.
Advancement.AdjustLedgerHint: The adjustment and its reason will be permanently added to the Experience ledger.
Advancement.AdjustmentIncomplete: Enter an amount of at least 1 XP and a reason for the adjustment.
Advancement.ZeroAdjustment: An Experience transaction must change the balance.
Advancement.LedgerHint: Awards and advancement spends are recorded automatically. Use Adjust XP for any game-specific or corrective transaction.
Advancement.NoLedgerEntries: No Experience transactions have been recorded yet.
Advancement.OpeningBalance: Opening balance carried forward when the Experience ledger was enabled.
Advancement.SpendHint: Choose an advancement for {actor}. Available XP: {current}.
Advancement.RestingConfirmation: The character is resting or advancing between sessions.
Advancement.TeacherConfirmation: A qualified teacher completed the required instruction. A non-magical Speciality's Persuasion roll succeeded; a magic teacher has a higher rank in the discipline.
Advancement.PrerequisiteHint: A Skill must have been used successfully since its last increase, unless a teacher with a higher rating instructed the character for one shift. New Skills selected from the world list require the teacher option; alternatively, drag the Skill to the Actor at rating 0 and mark its successful use.
Advancement.PrerequisiteDisabledHint: Successful-use requirements are disabled for this world. Non-magical Specialities still require a teacher and successful Persuasion; magical discipline ranks cost 10 XP with a higher-rank master or 30 XP without one.
Advancement.MagicSpecialtyOption: Learn {specialty} (10 XP with a master; 30 XP without)
Advancement.MagicRankOption: Increase {specialty} to rank {rank} (10 XP with a master; 30 XP without)
Advancement.SpecialtyTargetHint: Only Weapon Specialist requires this field. Enter the exact name of the Weapon type for this purchase; it is ignored for other advancements.
Advancement.NotAllowed: You do not have permission to manage advancement for this Actor.
Advancement.NoChoices: No Skill increases, new Skills, or new Specialities are currently available.
Advancement.RestRequired: Experience can only be spent while resting or between sessions.
Advancement.SkillAtMaximum: That Skill is already at its maximum rating.
Advancement.ActorSkillMissing: The selected Skill is no longer on the Actor.
Advancement.ActorSpecialtyMissing: The selected magical Speciality is no longer on the Actor.
Advancement.MagicRankMaximum: That magical Speciality is already rank 3.
Advancement.SkillPrerequisiteMissing: The Skill has not been used successfully since its last increase. Complete teacher instruction or mark a qualifying successful use first.
Advancement.NewSkillTeacherMissing: Learning a Skill directly from the world list requires instruction from a teacher. Alternatively, place it on the Actor at rating 0 and mark a qualifying successful use.
Advancement.SpecialtyTeacherMissing: Learning a Speciality requires a teacher, one shift of instruction, and a successful Persuasion roll by the teacher.
Advancement.NotEnoughXP: The Actor does not have enough XP for that advancement.
Advancement.SourceMissing: The source Item for that advancement is no longer available.
Advancement.AlreadyKnown: The Actor already has an Item with that name and type.
Advancement.SpecialtyTargetMissing: Weapon Specialist requires a Weapon Item name, and each target can only be learned once.
Advancement.Failed: The advancement could not be completed.
Advancement.IncreasedSkill: Increased {name} to {level} for {cost} XP. Its successful-use mark has been reset.

Questions.Participated: Did you participate in the game session?
Questions.Explored: Did you explore a new location?
Questions.DefeatedAdversary: Did you defeat one or more dangerous adversaries?
Questions.OvercameWithoutForce: Did you overcome an obstacle without using force?
Questions.FollowedTrait: Did you act according to your weakness, dark secret, big dream, or relationships?
Questions.FollowedConfiguredTraits: Did you act according to your {traits}?
Questions.ExtraordinaryAction: Did you perform another extraordinary action of some kind?

Combat.NotEnoughInitiativeCards: YZE initiative uses ten unique cards, including the extra cards drawn by Fast Reflexes. Group combatants or reduce participants until the required draws fit the deck.
Combat.NotEnoughActions: This combatant does not have the required actions remaining this round.
Combat.CannotExchangeInitiative: Initiative can only be exchanged at the start of this combatant's turn, before spending actions.
Combat.NoExchangeTargets: No combatant later in the current round is available for an initiative exchange.
Combat.ExchangeHint: Choose a combatant whose turn has not yet occurred. Their turn begins immediately after the exchange.
Combat.ExchangeResult: {source} exchanged initiative with {target}; {target} now acts immediately.
Combat.SelectOneTarget: Target exactly one token before making an attack.
Combat.NoAttackSkills: The attacker has no Skill Items available for the attack roll.
Combat.BrokenWeapon: This weapon has zero Reliability and cannot be used.
Combat.WeaponUnavailable: This weapon has no available quantity and cannot be used.
Combat.Aimed: Aimed shot (+2; consumes one Fast Action)
Combat.OverwatchAim: Overwatch aim (+2; the Fast Action was spent when overwatch was assumed)
Combat.DefenselessTarget: Target is defenseless or unaware (+3 where applicable)
Combat.BasicAttackHint: The system spends the attack's actions, ammunition, blocking reaction, cover, and armour in their SRD order.
Combat.AttackNegated: The attack inflicts no damage after opposing successes are applied.
Combat.UnarmoredDamageHint: Blocking removes attack successes. Ranged cover is rolled before equipped armour when damage is applied.
Combat.FinalDamageHint: The attack deals {damage} raw damage to {actor}. Enter the final amount after blocking, armour, cover, or other protection.
Combat.AttackTargetMissing: The targeted Actor is no longer available.
Combat.GMApplyDamage: You cannot update the target. A GM or an owner of the target must apply the damage.
Combat.ChooseConditionsHint: Choose exactly {count} new Physical Conditions for {actor}.
Combat.SelectConditionsCount: Select exactly {count} Conditions before applying damage.
Combat.DamageApplicationFailed: The attack damage could not be applied.
Combat.BlockFailed: The Block reaction could not be resolved.
Combat.TargetOwnerBlocks: Only a GM or an owner of the target can declare its Block reaction.
Combat.GMRequiredToLinkBlock: A GM must be connected to link a defender-owned Block roll to another user's attack message.
Combat.MeleeSkillMissing: The defender needs a Melee Skill Item to block.
Combat.ArmedBlockRequiresWeapon: An armed close-combat attack can only be blocked with a sturdy equipped weapon or tool.
Combat.DivingBlow: Diving blow (+2; attacker falls prone, and target also falls prone on a hit)
Combat.NotGrapplingTarget: A grapple attack can only be made against the opponent you are grappling.
Combat.SpecialAttackRequiresMelee: Special close-combat attacks and diving blows require the Melee skill.

SpecialAttacks.disarm: Disarm — wrest away a held item
SpecialAttacks.shove: Shove — push the target to Short range
SpecialAttacks.grappleStrike: Grapple attack — Fast Action, cannot be blocked

SpecialAttackResults.shove: {attacker} pushes {target} to Short range; move the token as appropriate.
SpecialAttackResults.grapple: {attacker} grapples {target}. Both fall prone and {target} drops held weapons.

Combat.RetreatNoEngagedEnemy: Retreat requires this Actor's active canvas token to be Engaged with at least one active hostile combatant and have no barrier between them.
Combat.RetreatFailed: {actor} retreats, but failed the Mobility roll. After the token moves, every Engaged enemy left behind makes an immediate free close-combat attack that cannot be blocked.
Combat.RetreatFreeAttackBegins: {attacker} makes a free close-combat attack against {target} with {weapon} after the failed retreat. This attack spends no action and cannot be blocked.
Combat.RetreatFreeAttackNoSkill: {attacker} cannot resolve the failed-retreat free attack automatically because the Actor has no Melee Skill Item.
Combat.NoOverwatchWeapon: Overwatch requires an equipped ranged weapon.
Combat.SimultaneousOverwatchOrder: {first} fires first. If that attack does not end {second}'s overwatch, {second} may then fire.

CharacterCreation.StepAllocationHint: Attributes start at C with three increases; one Attribute may be lowered to D for one extra increase. Choose one key Skill at B, two Skills at C and three at D.
CharacterCreation.NonDestructiveHint: Applying adds the selected starting options without removing existing Items.

CharacterCreation.NoSkills: No world Skill Items are available for character creation.

CharacterCreation.InvalidArchetype: This Archetype requires more choices than it provides. Correct its starting options before creating a character.
CharacterCreation.InvalidPoolAttributes: Assign exactly 14 Attribute points. Each Attribute must be 2–4, except the key Attribute which may be 5.
CharacterCreation.InvalidPoolSkills: Assign exactly 10 Skill points. Key Skills may be up to 3; other Skills may be up to 1.
CharacterCreation.InvalidStepAttributes: Use three net Attribute increases from C. No Attribute may exceed A, and at most one may be reduced to D.
CharacterCreation.InvalidStepSkills: Choose exactly one key Skill at B, two Skills at C and three Skills at D. All other Skills must have no rating.

WorldSetup.OverviewDice: Dice Pool or Stepped Dice for the core roll mechanic.
WorldSetup.OverviewDamage: Health, Resolve, Conditions, or Attribute Damage for harm.
WorldSetup.OverviewPushing: Bane damage, Stress Dice, Doom Points, and Conditions for pushing.
WorldSetup.Compendiums: All supplied SRD Actors, Items, Roll Tables, and Cards are available from the Compendium Packs tab. Import or drag only the content your world needs.
